title: Beginners Start Here | Hourglass
author: Sav
desc:
❣️Designed to build the appearance of perky heart-shaped glutes, and an hourglass shape from the front.

❣️ Pairs well with body recomposition or weight loss phases because it incorporates cardio progression. 

❣️ Add an optional deep core routine for a waist cinching look. 
3 x 30-45sec vacuums or hollow holds
3 x 16 dead bugs
3 x 10/side bird dogs
3 x 15 reverse crunches (optional)

❣️ Structured to build consistency and help you start (or restart) your fitness journey. 
💌 Starting small will help you to reframe movement as a lifelong habit. 
💌 8 weeks is enough time to fall in love with exercise and see results.

❣️ Great starting place to add more exercises you enjoy.

NOTES:

❕ Rep ranges: Begin toward the lower end of the listed rep range. As you get stronger, add reps while maintaining good form. Once you can reach the top of the range on all prescribed working sets, increase the weight slightly and work upward again.

❕ Effort: You do not need to train to failure. Especially during Weeks 1–2, aim to finish most sets feeling like you could perform another 2–3 good reps (2–3 RIR). As you readjust to training, most working sets can gradually move toward 1–2 RIR.

❕ Warm-up sets do not count as working sets. Before heavy exercises, perform enough lighter sets to feel prepared without tiring yourself out.

❕ Rest enough to perform well. Take approximately 2–3 minutes between demanding compound sets and 1–2 minutes between smaller/accessory exercises. Take longer if you need it.

❕ Progress > weight. Adding a rep with better technique, improving control or range of motion, or using slightly more weight are all forms of progress. Never sacrifice technique simply to increase the number on the machine/bar.

❕ Unilateral exercises: Listed reps are per side unless otherwise stated.

❕ Optional means optional! The purpose of this program is consistency. On low-energy or busy days, complete the required exercises and leave. Accessories can be added later as the habit becomes established.

❕ Exercise substitutions are okay. If an exercise causes pain, doesn’t suit your anatomy/equipment, or you don’t feel comfortable performing it, use a similar movement you can perform safely and consistently. Normal muscular effort is different from sharp or unusual pain.

❕ Cardio is progressive too. Start with the programmed duration/intensity rather than immediately doing more. Increase gradually as your conditioning improves, particularly if you are new or returning to exercise.

❕ Recovery matters. More training isn’t automatically better. Sleep, nutrition and recovery all affect performance and adaptation. If soreness/fatigue is consistently interfering with subsequent workouts, reduce volume or intensity rather than continually adding more.

❕ This is a starting point, not a forever program. After the 8-week reset, keep the movements you enjoy and consider gradually adding exercises or training days based on your goals, recovery and consistency.
